findings.title: Success criterion 5 has no serializer implementation task
findings.description: Description: Slice success criterion 5 (`project-documents/user/slices/313-slice.world-bounds-policy.md:365`) requires `config_to_yaml` to emit `WorldBoundsConfig.policy` as a plain string and for the emitted YAML to reload into an equal `ServerConfig`. The task file's "Files touched" list only assigns `config.py` work for "enum + field + loader validation" (lines 30-38), and Task 1.4 only asks for `test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip` to "assert policy matches" (line 88). There is no task to modify `config_to_yaml` serialization or assert the emitted YAML is plain-string/equal-config. This matters because the actual code needed a dedicated `_serialize_for_yaml` conversion before `yaml.dump` (`src/migratory_server/config.py:657-680`); a junior AI following the breakdown would not know to implement that. This leaves SC5's plain-string and equal-`ServerConfig` requirement unmet.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox lines instead of plain marker lines
findings.description: Description: All five commit markers at lines 96, 179, 249, 286, and 325 are written as `- [ ] **Commit:** ...` checkbox items. The review rule requires `**Commit**:` markers to be plain lines, never checkboxes; a file with no markers would be acceptable, so markers are not being required here. Placement at section boundaries is reasonable and is not "after every task" or "only at the end," but the format is wrong. Convert each to a plain `**Commit**: ...` line or remove the markers entirely.

findings.title: Integration test setup for one-step reflect is under-specified and can fail as written
findings.description: Description: Task 3.4 says to build a minimal `SimulationManager` with a 100×100 world, 4 agents, outward velocities, and `forces=[]`, then specifically asks `test_reflect_policy_flips_velocities_at_edges` to seed one agent at `(99, 50)` with velocity `(10, 0)`, step once, and assert `vx < 0`. The task does not specify `dt`, profile `max_speed`, `profile_indices`, or the `EntityManager` setup. With the common `dt=0.05` used in `tests/test_simulation.py:142`, the engine clamps velocity and then does `positions += velocities * dt` (`src/migratory/engine/integration.py:43-44`), so x becomes `99.5`, still inside a 100-wide world, and REFLECT never flips the velocity. A junior AI copying existing fixtures can produce a failing or non-isolating test. Specify a `dt` and seed state that guarantees an edge crossing on the first step, plus profile limits and state construction details.

findings.title: Task file is overweight for a 2/5 slice and includes low-value granularity
findings.description: Description: The task file is 334+ lines, has 23 top-level tasks, and lists 10 touched files for a slice marked effort 2/5. It is more detailed than the success criteria need: Task 2.3 enumerates roughly 18 unit tests (lines 147-172), Task 3.4 adds five more integration tests (lines 224-235), Task 3.5 and Task 5.1 both run the full pytest suite (lines 238-242 and 290-292), and finalization is split across Tasks 5.3-5.5 (lines 310-325). Several steps dictate implementation detail the slice does not require, such as exact `np.mod(..., out=...)`, boolean-mask mechanics, and the logger string. To fit the slice, merge Tasks 1.1-1.3 into one config implementation task, merge Tasks 4.1-4.2 into one shipped-config update task, keep a single final full-suite run, fold status/changelog/final commit into one finalization task, cut the redundant parametrized dispatch test at line 171 and duplicate single-step velocity-flip test at line 231, and reduce exact-code steps to observable success criteria.

findings.title: Traceability, sequencing, and test-with placement are otherwise sound
findings.description: Description: Apart from the SC5 serializer gap, the numbered success criteria have corresponding tasks: SC1-4 map to Tasks 1.1-1.4, SC6-9 to Tasks 2.1-2.3, SC10-11 to Tasks 3.2 and 3.4, SC12 to Tasks 4.1-4.2, SC13 to Tasks 3.5/5.1, and SC14 to Task 5.2. Dependencies are acyclic: config enum/field/loader → enforcement module → simulation wiring → shipped config defaults → final verification. Test tasks that exist immediately follow their implementation tasks (1.4 follows 1.1-1.3; 2.3 follows 2.1-2.2; 3.4 follows 3.1-3.3). The startup log line in Task 3.3 traces to the slice's Verification Walkthrough step 4, so it is not product scope creep; finalization/status work is process overhead, flagged separately for proportionality.

findings.title: No load-test or CI-gating gap is created
findings.description: Description: The slice does not restate a load/performance NFR that requires a `tests/load/` task. The only performance wording is qualitative ("performance cost ... negligible") around line 279, and the `OPEN` behavior is covered by Task 3.4's mock assertion that enforcement is not called. There is no `tests/load/` directory and no load-test task in this breakdown, so no CI wiring task is needed to gate on one; CI gating is not left implicit for a nonexistent load test.

structured_findings.summary: Success criterion 5 has no serializer implementation task
Commit markers are checkbox lines instead of plain marker lines
Integration test setup for one-step reflect is under-specified and can fail as written
Task file is overweight for a 2/5 slice and includes low-value granularity
Traceability, sequencing, and test-with placement are otherwise sound
No load-test or CI-gating gap is created
